questions.subject: science
questions.question: How many pairs of sex chromosomes are found in the human cell?
questions.explanation: Humans have one pair of sex chromosomes. This pair helps determine sex.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a chromosome made up of?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are made of DNA and protein. DNA carries hereditary information.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the main function of sex chromosomes?
options: To determine the structure of the eye
questions.explanation: Sex chromosomes decide male or female. They help determine sex.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the smallest unit of the chromosome that helps in the transmission of hereditary characteristics?
questions.explanation: Gene is the smallest hereditary unit. It passes characters from parents to children.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct for mitotic cell division?
options: Four cells are formed at the time of cell division.
Haploid cells are formed at the end of cell division.
It has the main role to form gametes.
This cell division helps to repair tissue.
questions.explanation: Mitosis makes new body cells. It helps growth and repair of tissues.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A technician exposed to radiation had reduced reproductive capacity. Which part of the cell is affected?
questions.explanation: Radiation can damage DNA. Damaged DNA can reduce reproductive capacity.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If the DNA transcription process is affected in a cell, which process is affected?
questions.explanation: DNA transcription helps make RNA for protein. If transcription is affected, protein synthesis is affected.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If a nucleotide is destroyed during DNA replication, what happens to the organism?
options: It brings a problem in cell division
It brings a problem in reproduction
questions.explanation: Damaged nucleotide can change DNA information. This may cause a genetic disorder.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which of the following indicates the set of chromosomes in a cell of a woman?
questions.explanation: A female has 44 autosomes and XX sex chromosomes. So the set is 44+XX.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?
options: Ovum contains only a Y chromosome and sperm contains an X chromosome.
Ovum contains only an X chromosome and sperm contains either an X or Y chromosome.
Ovum contains only an X chromosome and sperm contains a Y chromosome.
Ovum and sperm both contain X and Y chromosomes.
questions.explanation: Ovum always carries X chromosome. Sperm can carry X or Y chromosome.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which plant did Mendel use for his experiment?
questions.explanation: Mendel used pea plants. Pea plants have clear contrasting characters.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which of the following is the genotypic ratio for monohybrid cross?
questions.explanation: Monohybrid genotypic ratio is 1:2:1. It means pure dominant : hybrid : pure recessive.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the term for a characteristic that is passed down from generation to generation?
questions.explanation: Hereditary character passes from parents to offspring. It continues generation to generation.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A white-skinned child was born to dark-skinned parents. What is the reason for this?
options: Both father and mother have pure black characters
questions.explanation: Hybrid parents can carry hidden white character. So a white-skinned child may be born.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Farmers cross Boer goats with local goats to produce good meat. What kind of breeding method is this?
questions.explanation: Selective breeding chooses parents with useful traits. It is used to get better offspring.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A new plant produced by crossing an orange plant and a lemon plant is what type of plant?
questions.explanation: A hybrid plant comes from crossing two different plants. Orange and lemon crossing forms a hybrid.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A mule cannot give birth to a child. Which answer is correct?
questions.explanation: Mule is sterile. It cannot produce offspring naturally.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What are the two phases that complete mitosis and meiosis?
questions.explanation: Karyokinesis divides the nucleus. Cytokinesis divides the cytoplasm.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Where does mitotic cell division occur according to the chapter?
options: Only in mother cells of reproductive organs
In all cells of the body except reproductive cells
questions.explanation: Mitosis occurs in body cells. It does not usually occur in reproductive mother cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Where does meiotic cell division occur according to the chapter?
options: In all body cells except reproductive cells
In mother cells of major reproductive organs
questions.explanation: Meiosis occurs in reproductive mother cells. It forms gametes.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is formed at the end of mitotic cell division?
options: Two daughter cells with equal number of chromosomes
questions.explanation: Mitosis forms two daughter cells. They have the same chromosome number.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which symbol represents the chromosome number in body cells formed by mitosis?
questions.explanation: Body cells are diploid. Diploid chromosome number is written as 2n.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which significance of mitosis is mentioned in the chapter?
options: It plays a key role in physical growth
questions.explanation: Mitosis makes new cells for growth. So it helps physical growth.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How does mitosis help injured tissue?
options: It helps regenerate cells and return them to their original state
questions.explanation: Mitosis makes new cells at injured places. This helps repair tissue.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is meiosis called reductional division?
options: The chromosome number is reduced to half in daughter cells
It produces only two identical cells
It occurs only in blood plasma
questions.explanation: Meiosis reduces chromosome number to half. So it is called reductional division.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How many cells are finally formed from one diploid cell in meiosis?
questions.explanation: Meiosis forms four haploid cells. Haploid means half chromosome number.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What process in the first phase of meiosis brings variation?
questions.explanation: Crossing over exchanges parts of chromosomes. This creates variation.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement is a significance of meiosis according to the chapter?
options: It occurs in every body cell daily
It helps in evolution by bringing variation
questions.explanation: Meiosis brings variation in offspring. Variation helps evolution.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Where is DNA found in eukaryotic cells?
options: In the chromosomes of the nucleus
questions.explanation: In eukaryotic cells, DNA is inside chromosomes. Chromosomes are found in the nucleus.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is one nucleotide of DNA formed from?
options: Nitrogen base, deoxyribose sugar and phosphate
questions.explanation: A DNA nucleotide has base, sugar and phosphate. In DNA, the sugar is deoxyribose.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which nitrogen base is present in DNA but replaced by uracil in RNA?
questions.explanation: DNA has thymine. In RNA, thymine is replaced by uracil.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How is adenine linked with thymine in DNA according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: Adenine pairs with thymine by double bonds. This keeps DNA strands joined.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How is guanine linked with cytosine in DNA according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: Guanine pairs with cytosine by triple bonds. This makes the pair strong.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What main function of RNA is given in the chapter?
questions.explanation: RNA helps make protein. Protein is needed for body structure and functions.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which sugar is found in RNA?
questions.explanation: RNA contains ribose sugar. DNA contains deoxyribose sugar.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which are the three types of RNA mentioned?
questions.explanation: The three RNA types are mRNA, tRNA and rRNA. Each helps in protein synthesis.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which two main parts does a chromosome have according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: Chromosome has chromatid and centromere. Centromere joins chromatids.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a gene according to the chapter?
options: The smallest DNA segment on a chromosome that codes for a specific character
questions.explanation: A gene is a small DNA part on chromosome. It controls a specific character.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the main purpose of selective breeding?
options: To produce plants and animals with desired traits
questions.explanation: Selective breeding produces useful traits. Farmers use it for better plants and animals.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which method of selective breeding involves closely related animals producing offspring?
questions.explanation: Inbreeding is breeding between close relatives. It is one method of selective breeding.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How many pairs of chromosomes are found in human cells?
questions.explanation: Human body cells have 23 pairs of chromosomes. That means 46 chromosomes in total.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which chromosome set is found in male reproductive cells after meiosis?
questions.explanation: Male gametes are sperm. They can carry 22+X or 22+Y.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: When will a son be produced according to the sex determination chart?
options: When a 22+X sperm fuses with a 22+X ovum
When an ovum carries Y chromosome
When a 22+Y sperm fuses with a 22+X ovum
questions.explanation: A son is formed when Y sperm meets X ovum. This makes XY sex chromosomes.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the probability of getting a son or daughter after fertilization?
questions.explanation: Fertilization has equal chance of X or Y sperm. So chance is 50% son and 50% daughter.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which result did Mendel obtain in the F1 generation when pure tall and pure dwarf pea plants were crossed?
options: Half tall and half dwarf plants
questions.explanation: Tall character is dominant in Mendel's cross. So all F1 plants became tall.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In Mendel's monohybrid cross of tall and dwarf plants, what phenotypic ratio appeared in the second filial generation?
questions.explanation: In F2, tall and dwarf appeared in 3:1 ratio. Three were tall and one was dwarf.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What does Mendel's law of dominance state?
options: Only one character is expressed in F1 and it is called dominant
Recessive character is always expressed in F1
questions.explanation: Dominant character appears in F1. Recessive character remains hidden.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What does the law of purity of gametes explain?
options: Gametes contain both contrasting alleles together
Only dominant characters enter every gamete
Contrasting characters remain pure and separate during gamete formation
questions.explanation: Alleles separate during gamete formation. So each gamete gets only one allele.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What does genetic technology do at the gene level?
options: It modifies genes by adding, deleting or substituting DNA
questions.explanation: Genetic technology changes DNA at gene level. It can add, remove or replace DNA.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Where does fertilization take place in IVF according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: In IVF, fertilization is done in a laboratory. Egg and sperm are joined outside the body.
